doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Cecil Taylor date
summary: Terry joined an early avant-garde date with Rudd, Neidlinger and Moncur without knowing what it meant.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: You also worked with Cecil Taylor.

Yeah. Cecil Taylor and I did one of the first dates that the – years before the term “avant garde” was coined, this was the type of music that they were calling this in those days. Roswell Rudd, I think.
And what’s that – Mon – Grachan Moncur [drums].
Um-hmm. How did you relate to that music?

I don’t know. All I – I didn’t have any idea about categorization of the music, and this person and that person consider themselves this and that. I was just a trumpet player out there trying to get my thing together. Somebody who was connected with the record said to me, “Hey, we want you on this date with Cecil Taylor” and so forth. So I said, “Yeah, okay.” So next thing I knew, I was on the date. I had no idea what it meant, what it stood for, nothing. I didn’t even know how much money it paid.
